Bug: _sync_translation_permalink() called Permalink.save() without a savepoint; slug collision raised IntegrityError that poisoned the outer transaction on PostgreSQL (and on SQLite under Django TestCase's savepoint wrapping), causing TransactionManagementError on any subsequent ORM query. Bug: the AbandonedCheckoutEmailSend FAILED update in the MaxRetriesExceededError handler was inside the outer transaction.atomic() block; when send_campaign_email raised, that transaction was rolled back and the FAILED update was lost. The send row remained stuck at SCHEDULED; subsequent beat scans found it via get_or_create and never re-enqueued it. Fix: AbandonedCheckoutEmailSend.objects.filter(pk=send_id).update(status=FAILED) runs outside the rolled-back transaction in the MaxRetriesExceededError handler. Proof cycle: remove the update() line -> test FAILS (AssertionError: 'scheduled' != 'failed'); restore update() line -> test PASSES. Fix: campaigns/tasks.py send_abandoned_checkout_email MaxRetriesExceededError handler.

Bug: cart-CONVERTED race guard used filter(pk=send_id).update(CANCELLED) — only the directly processed send was cancelled. Sibling SCHEDULED sends (other email steps, same session) remained active indefinitely: the dedup row existed so beat never re-enqueued them, and the worker skipped them as SCHEDULED. Fix: filter(session=session, status=SCHEDULED).update(CANCELLED) bulk-cancels all sibling sends. Proof cycle: revert to filter(pk=send_id) -> test FAILS (AssertionError: 'scheduled' != 'cancelled' for send2); restore session-scoped filter -> test PASSES. Fix: campaigns/tasks.py send_abandoned_checkout_email cart_converted branch.

Bug: GET /checkout/resume/<token>/ advanced the campaign session IMPRESSION → INTERACTION unconditionally. Email link scanners (automated GETs) would trigger this without any human action, inflating INTERACTION counts and skewing recovery_revenue attribution. Fix: GET only advances NOT_STARTED → IMPRESSION; IMPRESSION → INTERACTION requires a POST (user clicking Proceed to Checkout). Proof cycle: revert _resume_get to advance IMPRESSION → INTERACTION on GET -> test_b6_get_does_not_advance_impression_to_interaction FAILS (AssertionError: 'interaction' != CampaignSessionState.IMPRESSION); restore POST-only INTERACTION gate -> test PASSES. The SENT status UPDATE had no store_id WHERE clause — tenant isolation guard was silently missing. Fix: .for_store(store).filter(pk=send_id).update(...) adds store_id to the WHERE clause. WHERE id=1); restore for_store(store) -> UPDATE SQL contains store_id AND id in WHERE clause -> test PASSES. Fix: campaigns/tasks.py send_abandoned_checkout_email step 7 SENT update.

Bug: accept_upsell computed idempotency_key but placed it only in the metadata dict; connector.capture_payment_intent and connector.create_off_session_charge were called without idempotency_key — both received the default '' value. Crash-retry re-issued full PaymentIntent.create / capture — double-charge risk. Fix: capture_payment_intent receives idempotency_key=f'capture:{order.pk}'; create_off_session_charge receives idempotency_key=f'upsell:{order.pk}:{step.pk}'. Proof cycle: remove idempotency_key kwargs from both connector calls in campaigns/upsell_service.py Phase B -> test_b1_capture_receives_deterministic_non_empty_idempotency_key FAILS (AssertionError: '' == '' — capture called without key); test_b1_off_session_charge FAILS likewise; restore both kwargs -> all 3 tests PASS. Fix: campaigns/upsell_service.py Phase B connector calls.

Bug: _watchdog_reconcile_stuck called capture_payment_intent directly without an atomic re-claim UPDATE; two overlapping watchdog runs could both call capture on the same stuck CAPTURE_IN_PROGRESS charge. Fix: atomic UPDATE capture_claimed_at=now WHERE status=CAPTURE_IN_PROGRESS first; if re_claimed != 1, return early. After the first call captures (status→CAPTURED), the second call's UPDATE WHERE status=CAPTURE_IN_PROGRESS finds 0 rows and returns early. Proof cycle: remove the re_claimed UPDATE + if re_claimed != 1: return block from campaigns/tasks.py _watchdog_reconcile_stuck -> test_b2_capture_called_exactly_once FAILS (AssertionError: 2 != 1 — capture called twice); restore block -> all 3 tests PASS. Fix: campaigns/tasks.py _watchdog_reconcile_stuck re_claimed guard.

Bug: accept_upsell used a single @transaction.atomic wrapping all phases; UpsellUnavailableError from Phase B rolled back accept_attempts F()+1 and the token's used_at — rate-limit was dead code and single-use tokens were replayable. Fix: three-phase structure (ADR-011 Fix 1): Phase A has its own committed with transaction.atomic() block before Phase B starts; Phase B failures cannot roll back Phase A's committed changes. Proof cycle: add @transaction.atomic decorator to accept_upsell and replace Phase A's with transaction.atomic(): with if True: -> test_b3a FAILS (AssertionError: 0 != 1 — accept_attempts rolled back); test_b3b FAILS (DoesNotExist not raised — token replayable); test_b3c FAILS (accept_attempts stays 0 across failures); restore three-phase structure -> all 4 tests PASS. Fix: campaigns/upsell_service.py Phase A isolation.

Bug: cart/checkout.py step 12b creates CampaignSession with no state= kwarg → defaults to NOT_STARTED. accept_upsell step 6 (upsell_service.py line 283) checks session.state != INTERACTION and raises UpsellUnavailableError (HTTP 410) — entire post-purchase upsell funnel was non-functional. Fix: campaigns/service.py serve_thank_you_step(order, store) performs an atomic conditional UPDATE NOT_STARTED → INTERACTION (with started_at=now), issues a fresh upsell-act token, and returns the step payload. Proof cycle: without fix serve_thank_you_step does not exist in campaigns.service → both tests fail with ImportError: cannot import name 'serve_thank_you_step' from 'campaigns.service'; add serve_thank_you_step to campaigns/service.py → both tests PASS (state transition verified, HTTP 200 from accept view confirmed). Fix: campaigns/service.py serve_thank_you_step.

Bug: accept_upsell Phase C (DB finalization) had no try/except. When Phase C failed after Phase B already captured money from Stripe, Phase C's savepoint rolled back and the UPSELL charge stayed AUTHORIZED with a placeholder PI id. The watchdog had no pass for UPSELL+AUTHORIZED charges, so would eventually void them — customers charged but goods not delivered. Fix 1: try/except around Phase C in campaigns/upsell_service.py; except block writes status=CAPTURED + real PI id outside the rolled-back savepoint. Fix 2: watchdog pass 6 in campaigns/tasks.py reconciles UPSELL+AUTHORIZED charges older than _STUCK_CAPTURE_MINUTES via retrieve_charge_by_idempotency_key. Proof cycle Fix1: remove rescue write body from except block (keep bare raise) -> test_phase_c_failure_leaves_charge_captured_not_authorized FAILS (AssertionError: 'authorized' != ChargeStatus.CAPTURED); restore rescue write -> PASSES. Proof cycle Fix2: remove pass 6 for-loop from capture_window_watchdog -> test_watchdog_pass6_recovers_orphaned_authorized_upsell FAILS (AssertionError: 'authorized' != ChargeStatus.CAPTURED); restore pass 6 -> PASSES. Fix: campaigns/upsell_service.py (Phase C try/except rescue write) + campaigns/tasks.py (pass 6 + _watchdog_reconcile_upsell_authorized).

Bug (docs/security/STATIC_PAGES_AUDIT.md F1): _validate_slug_not_reserved was attached to Permalink.slug ONLY as a Django field validator, which runs on full_clean()/ModelForm validation but NOT on Model.save(). Every real production write path (pages/signals.py sync_static_page_permalink via Permalink(...).save(), permalinks/signals.py handle_slug_change via a bare queryset .update()) bypassed it, so StaticPage.objects.create(slug='cart'/'fr', is_published=True) created an ACTIVE Permalink row that either 404s forever (shadowed by a fixed storefront/urls.py route) or collides with a language URL prefix. The pre-existing pages/tests/test_permalink_lifecycle.py::ReservedSlugAtPermalinkLevelTest only called Permalink.full_clean() directly and proved nothing about this bug (green before and after). Fix: (1) permalinks/models.py Permalink.save() calls _validate_slug_not_reserved(self.slug) before super().save() — the one place every permalink producer's .save() funnels through; (2) permalinks/signals.py handle_slug_change converted from a bare queryset .update(slug=new_path) to fetch+mutate+.save(); (3) pages/models.py StaticPage.clean() — same check at the ModelForm/admin boundary; (4) pages/models.py StaticPage.save() — same check directly in save(), before super().save(), so a bare StaticPage(...).save() raises with no row written at all. Proof cycle: commented out the _validate_slug_not_reserved call in Permalink.save() and both call sites in StaticPage.save()/StaticPage.clean() -> test_publish_cart_slug_rejected_and_no_permalink_created, test_publish_fr_slug_rejected_and_no_permalink_created, test_rename_to_reserved_slug_rejected_and_permalink_unchanged, and test_slug_hint_rename_to_reserved_value_rejected all FAILED (AssertionError: ValidationError not raised) while test_normal_slug_publishes_without_raising stayed green; restored all three enforcement points -> all 5 tests PASS. Fix: permalinks/models.py Permalink.save(), permalinks/signals.py handle_slug_change, pages/models.py StaticPage.clean()/StaticPage.save() (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

Bug (docs/security/STATIC_PAGES_AUDIT.md F2): storefront/views_pages.py _handle_contact_post/_handle_quotation_post and storefront/views_product_forms.py quotation_request_view/notify_me_view called .objects.create() with raw POST values and no length check; an over-length name/subject/customer_name/email would raise an unhandled DataError (HTTP 500) on the production PostgreSQL backend (SQLite silently accepts it, masking the bug in dev/test), and message (TextField) had no cap at all. Fix: each view now checks len(value) > Model._meta.get_field(name).max_length (introspected, cannot drift from the schema) for name/subject/customer_name/customer_email/email, and caps message against pages.antispam.PUBLIC_FORM_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH (5000); over-length input returns 400 with no row created, never 500. Proof cycle (SQLite cannot itself raise DataError, so the meaningful proof is 'reject + no row created' vs 'silently accept'): commented out the four length-check blocks in _handle_contact_post, _handle_quotation_post, quotation_request_view, and notify_me_view -> every '*_over_limit_*' test FAILED (response was the normal 302 success redirect and a row WAS created containing the full over-length value); '*_at_limit_*' tests stayed green throughout. Restored all four blocks -> all tests PASS. Fix: storefront/views_pages.py _handle_contact_post/_handle_quotation_post, storefront/views_product_forms.py quotation_request_view/notify_me_view (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

Bug (found while testing ADR-021's checkout activation ticket): stores.middleware.LocaleMiddleware wrote session['sf_lang'] unconditionally on every resolved request. The post-purchase upsell widget (storefront/templates/storefront/partials/upsell_widget.html) POSTs to the bare, un-prefixed /campaigns/upsell/accept/ or /campaigns/upsell/decline/ endpoint from the thank-you page, then calls window.location.reload() on the SAME thank-you URL (never navigating to a fresh /fr/... URL). That POST always resolves to the domain's ROOT language (campaigns/upsell/... is a fixed route mounted before any catch-all, exactly like /checkout/), so it silently overwrote the buyer's sf_lang session value with the root language; the widget's reload then re-rendered the thank-you page in English despite the buyer having browsed under /fr/. Fix: added "/campaigns/upsell/" to stores/middleware.py LocaleMiddleware.SF_LANG_WRITE_EXEMPT_PREFIXES (alongside the pre-existing /checkout/, /cart/, /search/, /orders/ entries added for the analogous checkout-language bug); also added "/products/" (notify-me/quotation POST endpoints) after a companion drift test (stores/tests/test_sf_lang_write_exemption_drift.py) found them uncategorized by the same walk. Proof cycle: remove "/campaigns/upsell/" from SF_LANG_WRITE_EXEMPT_PREFIXES -> both test_sf_lang_survives_upsell_decline_and_reload and test_sf_lang_survives_upsell_accept_attempt FAIL (AssertionError: 'Merci pour votre commande !' not found in ... — thank-you page re-rendered in English after the upsell POST + simulated reload); restore the entry -> both tests PASS. Fix: stores/middleware.py LocaleMiddleware.SF_LANG_WRITE_EXEMPT_PREFIXES (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

TEST_METHODS: N/A (no new test method — defensive teardown hardening only)
NOTES: Investigated a one-off test-order flake in chat.tests.test_tools + chat.tests.test_slot_provider reported during a full-suite run (green on all re-runs and in isolation; see docs/security/AI_CHAT_AUDIT.md flake section). Named hazard: core/tests/test_store_scoped_manager.py::StoreOwnedModelIsolationTest is a TransactionTestCase that flushes the whole DB after every test; the safety auditor hypothesized this leaves a stale ContentType.objects.get_for_model() cache entry (used by chat/localization.py:76 absolute_permalink_url and permalinks/signals.py:148) that would make a later chat test's permalink lookup silently return None if the polluter ran first in the same process. Reproduction attempt 1 (as specified): ran `manage.py test core.tests.test_store_scoped_manager chat.tests.test_tools chat.tests.test_slot_provider` 3x plus a full-suite run (2623 tests) -> all green every time, deterministically -- but this order never actually places the polluter before the chat tests: Django's DiscoverRunner.reorder_tests() always groups ALL TestCase-derived tests before ALL TransactionTestCase-derived tests regardless of command-line label order or --reverse (verified from django.test.runner source), so StoreOwnedModelIsolationTest structurally cannot execute before chat.tests.test_tools/test_slot_provider in a single manage.py test invocation, serial or --parallel (parallel dispatch is also strict FIFO by the same reordered list, and workers are separate processes so no cross-worker cache leak is possible either). Reproduction attempt 2 (forced): wrote a scratch custom test runner (not committed) that skips reorder_tests entirely, ran the modules in the literal given order (polluter first) -- test_get_product_same_store_returns_detail still PASSED. Reproduction attempt 3 (cache pre-warmed): ran test_tools once to warm the ContentType cache with the live pk, then the polluter class (5 flush cycles), then test_tools again -- still PASSED. Root cause of non-reproduction: django.contrib.contenttypes.management.create_contenttypes() -- invoked by the post_migrate signal that fires after every flush on this class, since available_apps is None and serialized_rollback is False, so inhibit_post_migrate is False -- calls ContentType.objects.clear_cache() itself before re-populating django_content_type, so the process-wide cache is already correctly invalidated on every flush cycle; there is no window where a stale pk can be read. Verdict: NOT_PROVEN as a live bug -- could not make the failure occur under any of the three attempts, including one that bypassed Django's own ordering guarantee entirely. Per the after-bug-test workflow, added ContentType.objects.clear_cache() defensively in StoreOwnedModelIsolationTest.tearDown() anyway (core/tests/test_store_scoped_manager.py, with a comment documenting this investigation and why it is believed unnecessary today), in case available_apps/serialized_rollback ever change on this class or Django's internal clear-on-post_migrate behavior changes. Full ordered-combo run (3x, 30 tests) and full suite (1x, 2623 tests) both OK after the change.

Bug: GiftCardTransactionInline and CampaignRewardInline (discounts/admin.py), shared by both DiscountCodeAdmin (store_admin_site) and DiscountCodeSuperAdmin (super_admin_site), had no get_queryset() override; TabularInline.get_queryset() fell back to the raising StoreScopedManager default manager (core/managers.py) for GiftCardTransaction/CampaignReward (both StoreOwnedModel), crashing the DiscountCode add/change form with IsolationError on either admin site while Django built the inline formset. The changelist-level version of this bug (DiscountCodeSuperAdmin.get_queryset) had already been fixed via cross_store_unsafe(); the inlines were explicitly left as a separate ticket. Fix: both inlines now override get_queryset() to return <Model>.objects.cross_store_unsafe(), matching the established convention for inlines shared across both admin sites (orders.admin.OrderItemInline/OrderFulfillmentInline, catalog.admin.CollectionProductInline) -- safe because Django's InlineModelAdmin further filters the rendered formset by the parent object's FK, so rows are always scoped to the one already-authorized parent DiscountCode. Also added has_add_permission()=False on both inlines (append-only/service-written records per each model's own docstring -- GiftCardTransaction and CampaignReward are never created manually). Proof cycle: removed both get_queryset() overrides from GiftCardTransactionInline/CampaignRewardInline in discounts/admin.py -> all 5 tests FAIL with core.managers.IsolationError ('Unscoped query on a StoreOwnedModel is forbidden') raised while building the inline querysets/formsets; restored both overrides -> all 5 tests PASS. NOTE: investigation surfaced a separate, unrelated, higher-severity bug -- DiscountCode.product_conditions/collection_conditions (plain M2M fields to catalog.Product/Collection, both StoreOwnedModel) crash EVERY DiscountCode change view via django.forms.models.model_to_dict() -> field.value_from_object() -> getattr(obj, attname).all(), invoked while building ModelForm(instance=obj), before inlines are even reached. Reproduced independently against discounts.GiftCardCampaign.trigger_products too (same M2M-to-StoreOwnedModel class of trap as GiftCardCampaignAdmin.save_related and engagement.service.resolve_excluded_paths, but on the read/model_to_dict path rather than the write/save_m2m path -- the existing save_related workaround does not cover it). Left unfixed as out of scope for this ticket; flagged for the orchestrator/Architect Agent as a follow-up (it blocks the DiscountCode and GiftCardCampaign change views outright, independent of this fix). Fix: discounts/admin.py GiftCardTransactionInline.get_queryset / CampaignRewardInline.get_queryset (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

Bug (WAVE3_AUDIT.md W3-1): out-of-order webhook delivery could flip a REFUNDED order back to PAID -- a fast refund-then-succeeded delivery (charge.refunded / PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REVERSED arriving before payment_intent.succeeded / PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED) accrued organization volume, fired purchase analytics, and enqueued gift-card issuance for an already-refunded order. Symmetrically, there was no whitelist on which statuses could transition to REFUNDED: a PENDING/FAILED/CANCELLED order could be flipped straight to REFUNDED by a premature refund event. Fix: 4 guards added, 2 per processor. Bug (docs/security/WAVE3_AUDIT.md §2.2): the public unauthenticated analytics beacon stored properties.page_version_id (and top-level product_id/collection_id/order_id) verbatim with no validation. The nightly aggregate_metrics command's raw-SQL CAST((properties->>'page_version_id') AS INTEGER) then raised "invalid input syntax for type integer" on PostgreSQL for any non-integer value ("abc", true, 1.5, a 2**70 int), killing _run_day -- and the whole --days N loop -- for every store, repeatably, for the poisoned row's entire 90-day retention. SQLite's CAST is lenient (returns 0), so the pre-fix suite stayed green on SQLite; this is explicitly NOT evidence for this bug class (see test module docstring). Fix (3 parts): (1) analytics/ingest.py _coerce_int_or_none() coerces properties.page_version_id and the top-level soft-id columns to int-or-None, rejecting bool, non-integer float, non-digit strings, and values outside the signed 32-bit range; non-coercible page_version_id is dropped from the stored dict entirely (never stored raw or as None), non-coercible top-level ids become NULL. (2) aggregate_metrics.py _json_int_expr() on PostgreSQL now emits CASE WHEN (col->>'field') ~ '^[0-9]{1,9}$' THEN CAST(...) ELSE NULL END instead of a bare CAST -- can never raise. (3) Command.handle()'s per-day loop wraps self._run_day(target_date) in try/except per day so one failing day cannot abort the remaining days of a --days N run. Proof cycle 1 (ingest coercion, 20 tests: CoerceIntOrNoneUnitTest all methods + IngestPageVersionIdCoercionTest all methods + IngestTopLevelSoftIdCoercionTest all methods): reverted _coerce_int_or_none to `return value` (no-op passthrough) -> 19 tests FAILED (AssertionError: e.g. 'True is not None', '1.5 is not None', '1180591620717411303424 is not None') and 1 ERRORED (test_order_id_huge_int_stored_as_null: Event.DoesNotExist -- the un-coerced 2**70 int passed to SQLite's INTEGER column raised OverflowError inside ingest_events' own try/except, silently dropping the ENTIRE batch, an even worse pre-fix outcome); restored _coerce_int_or_none -> all 20 tests PASSED. Proof cycle 2 (SQL-shape guard, 2 of 3 tests: JsonIntExprPostgresGuardTest.test_postgresql_expr_contains_case_when_regex_guard + test_postgresql_expr_has_no_bare_unguarded_cast; test_sqlite_expr_unchanged_lenient_cast is a control and is unaffected by this revert): reverted _json_int_expr's postgresql branch to a bare `CAST((col->>'field') AS INTEGER)` -> both tests FAILED ('CASE WHEN' not found in "CAST((properties->>'page_version_id') AS INTEGER)"; expr == bare_cast); restored the CASE WHEN guard -> both tests PASSED (control test passed throughout). Proof cycle 3 (per-day containment, 1 test: AggregateMetricsPerDayFailureContainmentTest.test_failing_day_does_not_abort_remaining_days): removed the try/except from Command.handle()'s per-day loop (bare `self._run_day(target_date)`) -> test ERRORED, RuntimeError('simulated poisoned-day failure') propagated out of call_command() uncaught; restored the try/except -> test PASSED (good day's AggregatedMetric rows written, bad day's absent, no exception propagated). PoisonedRowAggregationCoexistenceTest is included for coexistence/documentation only -- it runs on SQLite, whose lenient CAST was never the throwing side of this bug, so it passes identically with or without the _json_int_expr fix; it is NOT part of the PROVEN revert/restore evidence (see its own docstring), which rests on JsonIntExprPostgresGuardTest (SQL-shape) + the ingest-coercion tests (data never reaches the CAST as garbage) together, per the audit's own stated minimum bar. Full `analytics` app suite (118 tests) re-run after final restore: OK, no regressions. Fix: analytics/ingest.py _coerce_int_or_none/ingest_events, analytics/management/commands/aggregate_metrics.py _json_int_expr/Command.handle() (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

Bug (spec review, wave 3, finding #1): ProductPageVersion.clean() (catalog/models.py) only checked the reserved-slug/ISO-639 PATTERN for the composed slug f'{product_slug}-{suffix}', never whether that composed slug was already claimed by ANY OTHER active Permalink in the same (store, lang) -- Permalink's uniqueness is (store, lang, slug) regardless of content_type, so a version's composed slug can collide with an unrelated product, collection, static page, or another page version. That real collision escaped clean() entirely and only surfaced as an IntegrityError raised deep inside permalinks.registry.sync_page_version_permalinks() (called from the ProductPageVersion post_save signal, catalog/signals.py): an admin 500 through ProductPageVersionAdmin, and a silently ORPHANED ProductPageVersion row for any programmatic/autocommit .save() caller (script, AI persist path) that skips ModelForm.full_clean() -- by the time the post_save signal's IntegrityError fires, super().save() had already committed the ProductPageVersion row (no surrounding atomic block at that call site), leaving a version with no matching Permalink. Writing the admin-flow regression test also surfaced a second, independent, pre-existing bug: ProductPageVersionAdmin.raw_id_fields = ['product'] used Django's stock ForeignKeyRawIdWidget, whose label_and_url_for_value() looks up the currently selected Product via Product._default_manager (the raising StoreScopedManager, core/managers.py, ADR-001 Sec4) -- harmless on a blank add form, but ANY validation error that redisplays the form with the product field already filled in (including this ticket's own fix) crashed with IsolationError (500) while rendering the widget, which would have masked the very fix this ticket makes over real HTTP. Fix: (1) catalog/models.py ProductPageVersion._composed_slug_conflicts() -- new shared helper extending the per-language loop to also query for an existing active Permalink with the same composed (lang, slug), excluding this version's own permalink; clean() surfaces the first conflict as a slug_suffix field error (admin-form boundary), and save() now runs the SAME check itself, before super().save(), raising ValidationError instead of letting the row commit and orphan (mirrors pages/models.py StaticPage.save() -- the F1 security-audit precedent for this exact pattern). (2) catalog/admin.py -- added _StoreScopedForeignKeyRawIdWidget (overrides label_and_url_for_value to use Product.objects.cross_store_unsafe(), safe because it only decorates a PK the ModelForm's own store-scoped queryset independently validates, same 'relax the read, keep the write guarded' precedent as ADR-031/M2M-READ-PATH-ISOLATION) wired into ProductPageVersionAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey for the 'product' field. Proof cycle: temporarily disabled the new 'in_use' collision branch in _composed_slug_conflicts() (catalog/models.py) -> test_programmatic_save_rejects_collision_with_validation_error_and_no_orphan_row FAILED with an uncaught IntegrityError (ERROR, not the expected ValidationError) and test_admin_add_form_shows_field_error_not_500 FAILED (also ERROR, an uncaught IntegrityError over HTTP -- exactly the pre-fix 500); test_admin_add_form_without_collision_succeeds and test_programmatic_save_without_collision_still_succeeds stayed green throughout (sanity checks that the guard does not block non-colliding saves). Restored the branch -> all 4 tests PASS. Separately, reverted only the _StoreScopedForeignKeyRawIdWidget wiring (kept the slug-collision fix intact) -> test_admin_add_form_shows_field_error_not_500 FAILED with IsolationError (confirming the widget fix is independently necessary for the admin flow to ever return a 200 field error instead of a 500); restored the wiring -> test passed again. Fix: catalog/models.py ProductPageVersion._composed_slug_conflicts/.clean/.save, catalog/admin.py _StoreScopedForeignKeyRawIdWidget + ProductPageVersionAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

Stock label_and_url_for_value() resolves the selected object via Model._default_manager (the raising StoreScopedManager, core/managers.py, ADR-001 §4); harmless on a blank add form, but the first time the field re-renders WITH a bound value (any other field's validation error on the same form, or simply the initial GET of an existing object that already has the field set) 500s with IsolationError instead of showing the form/value. Inventory (raw_id_fields entries across every app; StoreOwnedModel targets only): campaigns/admin.py CampaignStepInline.accept_next_step/decline_next_step (-> CampaignStep), CampaignAdmin.entry_step (-> CampaignStep), CampaignStepAdmin.campaign (-> Campaign), CampaignSuperAdmin.entry_step (-> CampaignStep), CampaignStepSuperAdmin.campaign (-> Campaign); catalog/admin.py CollectionProductInline.product (-> Product), ProductPageVersionAdmin.product (-> Product, already fixed pre-sweep); aijobs/admin.py AiJobRunAdmin.job (-> AiJob), AiJobOutputAdmin.run (-> AiJobRun), AiJobValidationAdmin.run (-> AiJobRun); emails/admin.py SentEmailSuperAdmin.order (-> Order, dormant today since 'order' is always in SentEmailAdminBase.readonly_fields — fixed defensively so a future readonly_fields change can't resurrect the crash). Drift guard: core/tests/test_raw_id_widget_sweep.py introspects every ModelAdmin registered on both store_admin_site/super_admin_site plus every inline hung off `inlines = [...]`, finds every raw_id_fields entry whose FK target is a StoreOwnedModel, and calls formfield_for_foreignkey() directly to assert the widget is StoreScopedForeignKeyRawIdWidget — so a future admin that adds a raw_id field onto a StoreOwnedModel without wiring the safe widget fails this test immediately. Adjacent discovery while writing the campaigns HTTP tests: CampaignStepInline, AbandonedCheckoutEmailStepInline, and CampaignStepTranslationInline (campaigns/admin.py) had no get_queryset() override at all, so ANY GET/POST of a funnel or abandoned_checkout Campaign's change form (or a CampaignStep's own change form) 500'd via the raising default manager during Django's own initial_form_count()/media construction — entirely independent of raw_id_fields; filed and fixed here as CAMPAIGN-STEP-INLINE-ISOLATION (see that BUG_TESTS.csv row) because it blocked writing this ticket's own regression tests, not because it was in scope. A SECOND, much larger and NOT fixed here: Django's own BaseModelFormSet.add_fields() builds the hidden 'id' field for any EXISTING inline row via the target model's raw _default_manager, bypassing any admin get_queryset() override entirely -- POSTing an inline formset with >=1 existing StoreOwnedModel row 500s regardless of raw_id widgets, affecting essentially every StoreOwnedModel inline in the codebase (confirmed empirically against catalog's own ProductVariantInline on ProductAdmin, not just campaigns). Flagged as INLINE-FORMSET-PK-ISOLATION for Architect/Safety triage -- NOT fixed in this ticket (no BUG_TESTS.csv row: not yet proven/fixed, just discovered) since a proper fix needs a new shared inline-formset base class retrofitted across every StoreOwnedModel inline admin in the codebase, which is an architecture decision outside a widget-only sweep. Bug found while writing RAW-ID-WIDGET-ISOLATION's campaigns HTTP regression tests (unrelated to raw_id_fields itself): CampaignStepInline and AbandonedCheckoutEmailStepInline (both hung off CampaignAdmin/CampaignSuperAdmin) and CampaignStepTranslationInline (hung off CampaignStepAdmin/CampaignStepSuperAdmin) had NO get_queryset() override, unlike every sibling inline in the codebase (ProductVariantInline, ProductImageInline, CollectionProductInline all override it with .cross_store_unsafe()). Django's own InlineModelAdmin.get_queryset() default falls back to `self.model._default_manager.get_queryset()` -- the raising StoreScopedManager for these StoreOwnedModel targets -- so ANY GET or POST of a funnel-type or abandoned_checkout Campaign's change form, or of a CampaignStep's own change form, 500'd with IsolationError the moment Django built the inline formset's own initial_form_count()/media (before a single field was rendered). This is a complete, unconditional 500 for the affected admins in production today -- not an edge case. Also found and fixed in the same _FormsetWithDefaultPosition.add_fields() override (FR-B4/T039, CampaignStepInline.get_formset): (1) `index >= self.initial_form_count()` crashed with a bare TypeError when index is None (the JS 'empty form' template rendered via formset.empty_form, hit on every access to formset.media) -- guarded with `index is not None`; (2) the max-position lookup used `CampaignStep.objects.filter(campaign=obj).aggregate(Max('position'))` -- .filter() on the raising base manager, which does NOT actually raise for .aggregate() (a separate, NOT fixed here, gap in core/managers.py._RaisingQuerySet: .aggregate() bypasses __iter__/__len__/__bool__/_fetch_all and silently executes an unscoped cross-store query instead of raising IsolationError -- flagged for Architect/Safety triage as a hole in the ADR-001 §4 guarantee, confirmed via a throwaway reproduction: CampaignStep.objects.filter(campaign_id=999999).aggregate(Max('position')) returns cleanly instead of raising) -- fixed this one call site narrowly to `.for_store(obj.store).filter(...)` since obj (the Campaign being edited) is available, without touching the core manager. Proof cycle: temporarily removed CampaignStepInline.get_queryset() (restored the Django default) -> CampaignStepInlineBranchRawIdWidgetTest FAILED with IsolationError on GET; restored -> PASSED. Temporarily removed CampaignStepTranslationInline.get_queryset() -> CampaignStepAdminBranchRawIdWidgetTest FAILED with IsolationError on GET; restored -> PASSED. Temporarily removed the `index is not None` guard -> all three tests FAILED with a bare TypeError on GET (formset.media construction); restored -> all PASSED. Fix: campaigns/admin.py CampaignStepInline.get_queryset (new), CampaignStepInline.get_formset (aggregate scoping + None-index guard), AbandonedCheckoutEmailStepInline.get_queryset (new), CampaignStepTranslationInline.get_queryset (new) (pre-git, untracked WebsiteEcom directory).

Bug (ADR-031 addendum 2026-07-11, TICKET-051, flagged but explicitly NOT fixed by RAW-ID-WIDGET-ISOLATION's sweep): Django's own BaseModelFormSet.add_fields() (forms/models.py:1024-1028) builds the hidden 'id' field for an EXISTING formset row as ModelChoiceField(self.model._default_manager.get_queryset()) -- the raw manager singleton, bypassing every admin-level get_queryset() override entirely (including the .cross_store_unsafe() convention every StoreOwnedModel inline already used). For a StoreOwnedModel that manager is the raising StoreScopedManager (core/managers.py): on POST, ModelChoiceField.to_python() called queryset.get(pk=...) -> __len__ -> IsolationError, 500ing EVERY StoreOwnedModel inline POST that edits an existing row (confirmed empirically against catalog.ProductVariantInline before this ticket). The same add_fields() mechanism is reused by modelformset_factory() for list_editable changelists -- a third surface, live on currency.StoreCurrencySettingAdmin (list_editable=['is_enabled']), whose bulk-save POST 500'd identically. The ADR-031 M2M relation-bound relaxation (core/managers.py StoreScopedManager.get_queryset()) cannot fix this: that detection keys off .instance/.through being set on the MANAGER instance used for the read; here the manager is the bare class-level _default_manager singleton with neither attribute set -- no manager-level signal exists to detect 'this call originates from a formset's add_fields()'. Fix: core/formsets.py (new) StoreSafePKFormSetMixin swaps the pk field's queryset for the formset's own already-scoped self.queryset -- relation/scope-safe by construction on both paths (BaseInlineFormSet.__init__ filters by the parent FK; changelist_view builds the changelist formset's queryset from ModelAdmin.get_queryset(request)), only when the stock queryset is a _RaisingQuerySet over self.model (leaves the OTHER add_fields() branch -- taken when the model's own primary key IS itself an FK/O2O -- deliberately unrelaxed and still raising; pinned as safe today by drift test (c), since no StoreOwnedModel currently has such a primary key). StoreSafeInlineFormSet / StoreSafeModelFormSet wire the mixin onto BaseInlineFormSet / BaseModelFormSet respectively. core/admin.py (new) StoreOwnedInlineMixin bundles formset=StoreSafeInlineFormSet with the established get_queryset()->cross_store_unsafe() convention (previously copy-pasted independently across orders/catalog/discounts/campaigns/chat/engagement/pages/cart/shipping inlines -- this family had bitten five times before this ticket, per BUG_TESTS.csv's own RAW-ID-WIDGET-ISOLATION and CAMPAIGN-STEP-INLINE-ISOLATION rows); migrated all 21 grep-found inline classes onto it (18 target StoreOwnedModel subclasses and now use the mixin; the other 3 -- currency.CurrencyRateInline, payments.OrgPoolMemberInline, payments.ProcessorOptionInline -- target plain, non-StoreOwnedModel models and are correctly left untouched). Migrating onto the mixin incidentally fixed two previously undiscovered latent isolation bugs where NO get_queryset() override existed at all (shipping.ShippingRateExceptionInline, chat.ChatMessageInline -- both StoreOwnedModel targets, both would already 500 on any GET/POST with an existing row, untested until now). campaigns.CampaignStepInline's dynamically-built _FormsetWithDefaultPosition (FR-B4/T039) re-parents onto StoreSafeInlineFormSet automatically, since Django's inlineformset_factory always subclasses self.formset and _FormsetWithDefaultPosition subclasses whatever get_formset() returns. currency.StoreCurrencySettingAdmin.get_changelist_formset injects StoreSafeModelFormSet. Bonus tightening (documented risk, not a behavior change for any legitimate request): pk validation now rejects any pk outside the formset's own scoped queryset instead of stock Django's 'any row in the whole table' -- closing a minor IDOR probe surface. Two related, out-of-scope bugs surfaced (not fixed here) while writing the pk-tamper test on ProductVariantInline: (1) catalog.models.py ProductVariant.clean() crashed with RelatedObjectDoesNotExist (self.store unset) when a tampered pk causes Django's BaseModelFormSet._construct_form() to fall back to a brand-new blank instance still populated from the row's OTHER submitted fields -- fixed narrowly (guarded self.sku and self.store_id, in scope: this IS the pk-tamper cleanliness the addendum's test #3 requires) since the row is never persisted either way (the pk field's own error blocks the save) and the DB UniqueConstraint remains the belt-and-suspenders check for any row that IS store-assigned; (2) core.widgets.CsvListWidget (ProductAdminForm.Meta.widgets['tags']) is incompatible with django.forms.JSONField .bound_data() -- ANY validation error anywhere on ProductAdminForm forces a bound-form re-render, which crashes with TypeError('the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not list') because CsvListWidget.value_from_datadict() returns an already-parsed list (needed for JSONField.to_python() to accept it at clean time) but JSONField.bound_data() unconditionally json.loads()s that same value for redisplay -- entirely unrelated to store isolation, never previously exercised by any full HTTP POST test against /admin/catalog/product/.../change/, NOT fixed here (belongs in core/widgets.py, a widget/field redesign decision outside this ticket), flagged for a follow-up ticket; the PK-tamper proof was moved to CampaignStepInline instead, whose parent admin form has no such widget. Proof cycle: reverted `formset = StoreSafeInlineFormSet` from StoreOwnedInlineMixin (core/admin.py) and the StoreSafeModelFormSet injection in currency.StoreCurrencySettingAdmin.get_changelist_formset -> ProductVariantInlinePostRegressionTest, CampaignStepInlinePostRegressionTest (all 3 methods), StoreCurrencySettingChangelistPostRegressionTest (both methods), and the two InlineFormsetStoreSafeSweepTest/ChangelistFormsetStoreSafeSweepTest drift tests ALL FAILED (500 IsolationError on the POST tests; named-failure assertions on the drift tests) -> restored both -> all PASSED. NOTES: Bug (ADR-031 addendum 2026-07-11, 'AGGREGATE-DOESNT-RAISE and its full family', TICKET-051): core.managers._RaisingQuerySet only overrode __iter__/__len__/__bool__/_fetch_all -- several QuerySet terminal methods execute SQL directly without ever calling any of those four, silently bypassing the ADR-001 §4 isolation guard entirely: aggregate() (query.get_aggregation directly), count() (query.get_count directly), exists() (query.has_results directly, and via it contains()), iterator() (self._iterator directly, a distinct generator from __iter__), aiterator() (builds self._iterable_class directly, NOT via iterator() -- needs its own override), update() (compiler.execute_sql directly -- A SILENT UNSCOPED CROSS-STORE WRITE, the worst member: discounts/service.py's §XIII atomic coupon/gift-card decrements ran as DiscountCode.objects.filter(pk=...).update(...) for months, working only BECAUSE of this hole), the fast-delete path of delete() (Collector.can_fast_delete() skips fetching objects, so it never touches _fetch_all() either), and explain(). First found narrowly (one aggregate() call site) while writing CAMPAIGN-STEP-INLINE-ISOLATION's regression tests; this ticket closes the whole family. Fix: _RaisingQuerySet now overrides aggregate/count/exists/iterator/aiterator/update/delete/explain to raise IsolationError unconditionally (aiterator as a plain non-async-generator method -- raising eagerly and synchronously before any `async for` begins is simpler than reproducing Django's async-generator shape and equally effective). contains() and bulk_update() deliberately do NOT get their own override -- Django's own implementations delegate to exists()/update() respectively on a self.filter()/self.using() clone that PRESERVES this class, so the raise already happens transitively; pinned by an explicit test rather than merely assumed, per the addendum's own Risks section. Added the one sanctioned safe entry point, StoreScopedManager.none(), returning a real (non-_RaisingQuerySet) empty queryset -- fixes, in one change with no call-site edits needed anywhere, a pre-existing booby trap in EVERY admin get_queryset(request) no-store fallback across the codebase (~30 call sites, e.g. DiscountCodeAdmin.get_queryset, StoreCurrencySettingAdmin.get_queryset): Model.objects.none() previously resolved via the manager's auto-generated queryset-method proxy to self.get_queryset().none(), a _RaisingQuerySet clone whose __iter__ etc. still unconditionally raised despite the query being empty; defining none() directly on StoreScopedManager overrides that proxy via normal Python subclass method resolution. NOTES: Bug (ADR-031 Addendum 3, 2026-07-11, 'the validation ring', TICKET-052; trigger: TICKET-051's terminal-method closure turned the suite red, 27/28 failures, one root cause). Model validation was never isolation-safe; it worked for months only because exists() silently bypassed the raise. Four internal Django paths query through Model._default_manager (NOT _base_manager) and terminate in the newly-raising exists()/count(): (1) Model._perform_unique_checks (base.py:1538) -> model_class._default_manager.filter(**lookup_kwargs).exists() -- breaks full_clean()/admin validation for every unique_together/unique=True on a StoreOwnedModel; (2) Model._perform_date_checks (base.py:1579), same shape, no unique_for_* exists today but covered by the same window; (3) UniqueConstraint.validate (constraints.py:573) -- model._default_manager.using(using)...exists(), no queryset-injection hook exists in its signature; (4) ModelChoiceIterator.__len__/__bool__ (forms/models.py:1455,1458) over the stock FK/M2M formfield queryset (the raw _default_manager.using(using), related.py:1208,2048) -- rendering ANY admin FK/M2M widget with no explicit queryset override crashes the same way. Meta.base_manager_name is doubly irrelevant: all four paths use _default_manager, and _base_manager is already an auto-created plain Manager when base_manager_name is unset. Constraint enumeration confirmed: every unique_together/UniqueConstraint on every StoreOwnedModel names or transitively pins 'store' -- no store-independent (global) constraint exists today, but the chosen fix preserves stock Django semantics so a future global constraint would validate correctly cross-store without revisiting this ADR. Fix D1 (core/managers.py, core/models.py): a contextvars.ContextVar window (_MODEL_VALIDATION_WINDOW) that unlocks ONLY _RaisingQuerySet.exists(), opened for the exact duration of the new StoreOwnedModel.validate_unique()/.validate_constraints() wrapper methods' own super() call (try/finally, exception-safe). update()/delete()/count()/aggregate()/iteration all keep raising even while the window is open (pinned explicitly by ValidationWindowNarrownessTest.test_window_unlocks_only_exists_not_count_or_update, which forces the contextvar open directly and asserts count()/update() still raise on the identical queryset). The window does not leak into user clean() code: full_clean() runs clean_fields() then clean() BEFORE validate_unique() opens the window, pinned by test_unscoped_clean_still_raises_isolation_error using a test-only StoreOwnedModel (WindowProbeWidget, @isolate_apps('core'), mirrors core/tests/test_store_scoped_manager.py's TestProduct pattern) whose clean() deliberately performs an unscoped .exists() and must still raise IsolationError. Cross-store duplicates remain allowed / in-store duplicates remain rejected (constraint semantics unchanged, only the query MECHANISM was unblocked) -- proven on a second test-only model (SemanticsProbeWidget) with the same slug on two different stores validating cleanly, and the same slug on the same store raising a plain Django ValidationError (not IsolationError). Two full-HTTP admin POST regressions added: discounts.DiscountCodeSuperAdmin (super_admin_site) duplicate (store, code) ADD POST -> clean form error, not 500 (pages.StaticPage was tried first per the ADR's own example and does NOT work through the real admin -- see finding below); engagement.SocialProofSettingsAdmin duplicate-per-store ADD POST -> clean UniqueConstraint error, not 500. Fix D2 (core/admin.py StoreScopedFormFieldsMixin; webecom/admin.py _StoreScopedRegistrationMixin): shared formfield_for_foreignkey/formfield_for_manytomany default-queryset backfill for any FK/M2M field targeting a StoreOwnedModel with no explicit queryset override -- store site: .for_store(request.store) (or .none() if request.store is absent); super site: .cross_store_unsafe(), narrowed to a bound instance's own store via request.resolver_match.kwargs['object_id'] when this is a non-inline ModelAdmin (TICKET-050 GiftCardCampaignAdmin precedent) -- inlines are left unfiltered on the super site since object_id there names the PARENT, not self.model. Bug (ADR-032, Django 6.0.4 source-traced): every store-admin-site ModelAdmin excludes 'store' from the form (assigned in save_model(), AFTER form.is_valid() already ran per contrib/admin/options.py:1847-1853) -- two INDEPENDENT kill switches then silently drop any store-inclusive unique_together/UniqueConstraint check: (1) BaseModelForm._get_validation_exclusions() adds 'store' to exclude because it isn't a form field, and Model._get_unique_checks()/UniqueConstraint.validate() both drop/skip any check touching an excluded field; (2) even without exclusion, Model._perform_unique_checks() skips any lookup whose value is None, and instance.store_id is None at validation time regardless. A same-store duplicate submitted through the real admin HTTP endpoint sailed through form.is_valid() and then 500'd with a raw IntegrityError at save_model()'s INSERT -- confirmed by direct reproduction on pages.StaticPage during TICKET-052 (documented in core/tests/test_validation_window_isolation.py's DiscountCodeUniqueTogetherAdminPostTest docstring as a separate, out-of-scope finding routed to the Architect Agent). D4 (deliberately NOT built): a global IntegrityError catcher -- rejected per ADR-032 Options (c); the residual post-validation TOCTOU race (two concurrent identical submissions) is accepted as stock-Django posture. ADR-033 D5b: a store must never transition from >=1 to 0 active full-access employees via demote/deactivate/delete on the store site. Proof cycle: commented out the `self._validate_lockout_guard()` call inside StoreEmployee.save() (stores/models.py) -> test_demote_last_full_access_employee_is_blocked and test_deactivate_last_full_access_employee_is_blocked FAIL (ValidationError not raised, employee.full_access/.is_active flips with no guard), and the sequential-demote proof in StoreEmployeeLockoutConcurrencyTest FAILS ('blocked' not found in 'demoted' for the second demote) -> restored the guard call -> all three PASS. Backend caveat: this project's test settings use in-memory SQLite, which does not implement true row-level locking (select_for_update() is a documented no-op there); the concurrency test therefore proves the guard's check-then-act correctly reads COMMITTED state across two writers run in sequence, not true interleaved-thread lock contention (that requires Postgres, used in production).

Bug found while implementing ADR-033's request-cached StoreEmployee resolver (stores/permissions.py get_store_employee): the original implementation used hasattr(request, _CACHE_ATTR)/getattr(...)/setattr(...) to cache the lookup on the request object. A MagicMock request (the prevailing pattern across this codebase's admin permission tests) auto-vivifies ANY attribute access, so hasattr(mock, '_pradize_store_employee_cache') is ALWAYS True even before the cache is ever written, and getattr() returns a fresh, truthy MagicMock instead of None/the real employee -- check_module_access then read employee.full_access (an auto-mocked, truthy attribute) and incorrectly GRANTED access to users with no StoreEmployee row at all. Proof cycle: reverted get_store_employee to use hasattr/getattr/setattr instead of request.__dict__ -> many badges/engagement/pages permission tests using MagicMock requests started asserting True where False was expected (e.g. 'no employee row denies everything') -> restored the request.__dict__-based cache check -> all tests pass. Fix: stores/permissions.py get_store_employee() checks `_CACHE_ATTR in request.__dict__` / `request.__dict__[_CACHE_ATTR]` directly, bypassing the attribute-access protocol Mock overrides.

Pre-existing latent bug found while migrating campaigns/admin.py onto the shared resolver (ADR-033 D3a): CampaignAdmin.has_change_permission/has_delete_permission and CampaignStepAdmin.has_change_permission/has_delete_permission called super().has_change_permission(request, obj) for the non-platform-campaign branch. WAVE 4 Safety Agent audit F-1 (docs/security/WAVE4_AUDIT.md): StoreEmployee._validate_lockout_guard() (stores/models.py) locked the qualifying set with .exclude(pk=self.pk) chained onto the select_for_update() queryset itself -- excluding self from the LOCK, not just the count. Two concurrent demotes of a store's last two active full-access employees (e.g. A demotes B, B demotes A) each locked the OTHER row only -- disjoint row sets never contend, select_for_update never serializes them, both transactions see 'another qualifying row exists', and both commit, leaving the store with ZERO active full-access employees (defeats ADR-033 D5b). Fix: the locking SELECT now filters only on store_id/full_access/is_active (no .exclude on the locking queryset at all, so self's own still-qualifying-in-the-DB row is included in the lock); the self-exclusion for the 'is there another qualifying row' COUNT moved to a plain Python any(row.pk != self.pk ...) check over the already-locked, materialized row list. The delete path (stores/admin.py delete_model/delete_queryset) was already correct (locks the whole store set, no exclude) and needed no change. Two tests, replacing the old same-named test that ran 't1.start(); t1.join(); t2.start(); t2.join()' fully sequentially and so passed even with the bug present (it only proved the unlocked pre-check blocks a SECOND demote after the FIRST already committed): (1) test_concurrent_demotes_barrier_synced_real_lock_contention -- genuine two-thread, Barrier-synchronized concurrency test, skip-guarded to Postgres only (connection.vendor == 'postgresql') because this project's test settings use in-memory SQLite, whose select_for_update() is a documented Django no-op (plain SELECT, never blocks) -- on SQLite neither thread's read ever waits on the other regardless of query shape, so the test cannot distinguish fixed from buggy there and is skipped rather than passing by luck; (2) test_lockout_guard_lock_query_includes_self_row_not_just_others -- deterministic, backend-independent structural proof that always runs (including plain CI on SQLite): captures the actual SQL issued by the locking SELECT via CaptureQueriesContext and asserts it contains no '"id" = <self.pk>' predicate (which is exactly what .exclude(pk=self.pk) on the locking queryset compiles to). Proof cycle: reverted the fix (locking query rebuilt with .select_for_update().filter(store_id=..., full_access=True, is_active=True).exclude(pk=self.pk).exists()) -> test_lockout_guard_lock_query_includes_self_row_not_just_others FAILS (AssertionError: '"id" = 1' unexpectedly found in the captured locking SELECT's WHERE clause); restored the fix -> test PASSES. Fix: stores/models.py StoreEmployee._validate_lockout_guard().
